title: Sparse-topic multilingual probe notes and sanity checks
content:
Purpose:
This note collects an actionable evaluation set and lightweight probe checklist for two related onboarding concerns we repeatedly see when accepting embedding models: 1) sparse-topic coverage (long-tail topical buckets with few exemplars) and 2) multilingual neighborhood alignment. The goal is a compact, reproducible evaluation that surfaces cluster sanity issues and cross-lingual drift before models are promoted for production semantic search or embedding-based retrieval.

Scope and key questions:
- Semantic search relevance: do nearest neighbors (NNs) reflect topical relevance across short queries and long-form queries?
- Clustering sanity: for sparse topics, does the embedding geometry separate topic islands (avoid hubness) and preserve local structure?
- Multilingual alignment: are translations and transliterations colocated in embedding space (same-topic items in different languages are near each other)?
- Robustness to noise: how much label/phrasing noise causes rank/order inversion for top-k retrieval?

High-level dataset composition (compact probe set):
- Sparse topical buckets: 40 topics with skewed counts: 25 topics with 3–6 exemplars, 10 topics with 7–15 exemplars, 5 dense control topics with 50+ exemplars. Topics sampled from: product help articles, niche Wikipedia stubs, specialized forum threads (e.g., hardware repair), and legal clause snippets.
- Multilingual parallel items: a subset of 300 items translated across 5 languages (en, es, fr, de, pt). For each item we include: canonical English sentence, professional translation (if available), back-translation check, and a short paraphrase.
- Noise injections: synthetic perturbations applied to 20% of queries (character swap, punctuation removal, abbreviations, numeric obfuscation) and 10% of corpus items (truncation, HTML artifacts, markup).
- Query types: short keyword queries (1–3 tokens), natural-language questions (8–20 tokens), and long prompts (30–120 tokens).

Sampling procedure (reproducible):
1. Source raw corpora: wikipedia-stubs-2024 (topic seed), internal-help-compact-2024 (product docs), forum-sampled-2023 (public forum snippets).
2. Topic seed selection: pick topically distinct seeds by TF-IDF centroids, then manually prune near-duplicates.
3. For each seed, sample exemplars by document-level stratified sampling (prefer short docs for sparse topics, long docs for dense controls).
4. Generate parallel translations using vendor-translated subset + MLT (machine translation) for remainder, mark quality with a translation_quality tag (human/reviewed | machine).
5. Persist as a line-delimited JSONL with fields: id, topic_label, source, language, text, translation_group_id, quality_flag, noise_variant (if applicable).

Evaluation probes and metrics (compact battery):
- Neighbor recall (NR@k): fraction of true-topic items appearing in top-k neighbors for each query. Use NR@10 and NR@50; target for sparse topics: NR@10 >= 0.18 (baseline), NR@50 >= 0.45.
- Mean reciprocal rank (MRR): for canonical retrieval ordering across query types. Monitor MRR drop between clean and noisy variants.
- Silhouette coefficient (cluster-level): measure separation of topic clusters; for sparse topics, expect silhouette > 0.05 (low but positive). Large negative values indicate mixing/hubness.
- Pairwise angular distance drift: compare average angular distance between translation pairs vs same-language pairs; acceptable parity: translation_pair_distance <= same_language_distance + 0.02.
- Hubness score (k-occurrence distribution): count tokens/documents that appear disproportionately in many nearest neighbor lists; flag when top-1% accounts for > 8% of NN occurrences.
- Stability under noise (perturbation recall delta): absolute drop in NR@10 between clean and noisy query <= 0.10 for acceptable models.

Probe definitions (concrete examples):
- Topic probe: Query = "remove battery macbook pro 2015"; expected neighbors: repair-guides, teardown paragraphs, battery-safety steps across languages.
- Translation probe: English sentence + Spanish translation; check whether top-5 neighbors include both.
- Sparsity probe: topic with 4 exemplars about "vintage fax machine troubleshooting"; measure whether exemplars cluster tightly or are pulled toward dense electronics topics.
- Ambiguity probe: short-token query that is polysemous (e.g., "spring"), verify cluster assignments align with disambiguation context when longer query provided.

Acceptance criteria (suggested thresholds for promotion):
- Overall NR@10 across all sparse topics >= 0.20.
- Translation pairing precision@5 >= 0.65 for human-reviewed translations.
- Hubness: top-1% NN participants account for <= 6% of occurrences.
- Noise stability: median NR@10 drop <= 0.08.
- Manual spot checks: for 20 randomly sampled sparse topics, human reviewer agrees with top-5 neighbors for >= 14 topics.

Quick-run checklist (developer playbook):
1. Checkout embedding-evals repo and pull PR branch noted in linked_artifacts.
2. Prepare embeddings: run embedder on corpus with same batching/quant settings used in onboarding. Save tensors in npy (id order persisted).
3. Run probe runner: python tools/probe_runner.py --corpus corpus.jsonl --embeddings corpus.npy --queries probes.jsonl --k 50 --metrics nr,mrr,silhouette,hubness --out results/<model>-probe.json
4. Generate HTML spot-check page: scripts/render_spot_checks.py results/<model>-probe.json --output results/<model>-spotchecks.html
5. Open results and attach spotchecks to onboarding ticket (AI-4021).

Known limitations and caveats:
- Translation quality: machine-translated items can bias alignment metrics; always segment human-reviewed parallel subset and report both numbers.
- Topic granularity: sparse topics are intentionally narrow; some models intentionally map narrow topics closer to more generic clusters for smoothing — acceptable if downstream user intent is satisfied, but must be documented.
- Batch/quantization mismatch: embedding deviation caused by int8 quantization or kernel changes can dominate subtle topology issues; run both float and quantized probes if model will be deployed quantized.

Open items / next steps:
- Finalize the canonical sparse topic list (link to spreadsheet in linked_artifacts) and lock translations by 2025-10-10.
- Add an automated nightly check that runs the compact probe on all staging models and surfaces regressions > 10% NR@10 drop on slack #embeddings-alerts.
- Run cross-model comparisons with existing Redwood-verified model catalog to calibrate acceptance thresholds (schedule: Q4 2025).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add a short script to compute hubness per-topic rather than global hubness (helps locate offending docs).
- Try contrastive re-ranking baseline (dot product score rescaling) on a sampled sparse topic to see if normalization reduces hubness.
- Collect human-annotated judgments for 200 translation probe pairs (budget: 2–3 hrs on internal reviewers).

References and links: see linked_artifacts for eval code PR and onboarding ticket. For background reading: Arora et al. "On the geometry of embeddings and downstream retrieval" (working notes), internal note on "embedding hubness mitigation" in shared drive (search: hubness-mitigation-2024).

Appendix: minimal file format example (jsonl):
{"id":"sparse_0001","topic_label":"vintage_fax_repair","source":"forum-sampled-2023","language":"en","text":"How to clear fax memory on a 1997 Panaso...","translation_group_id":"tg_041","quality_flag":"machine","noise_variant":"clean"}

End of probe notes.
